clue.text: Points in motor-vehicles touch lightly

indicators.note: the points are placed inside the word for the vehicles, so in signals one piece going within another

parts.note: motor-vehicles are cars
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A remark about the contact points in motor cars that only brush against something.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle stroke of affection is exactly a light touch, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Chap on foot. Bill, in trouble in links

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for the links, so in signals a container

parts.note: a chain is a series of links

indicators.note: the name's letters are in disorder, so in trouble signals an anagram

explanation.surface: A man walks on foot, and Bill is in trouble on the golf links.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' scrambles the name to ILBL. 'Chap' is the verb sense, skin cracked by cold, not a man, and the links are not a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilblain is an itchy sore from cold, chapped skin, typically on the toes.

clue.text: Put back foreign currency after a holiday

indicators.note: the currency piece comes after the holiday piece in the answer

parts.note: a rest is a holiday or break
the öre is a small coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: Someone changes back their leftover foreign money after a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To return something to its former place or condition is to replace it.

clue.text: Steps taken to avoid pieces of fencing?

definitions.text: Steps taken to avoid pieces of fencing?

parts.words: Steps taken to avoid pieces of fencing?
parts.note: steps are dance steps, and the pieces of fencing are not fence panels but blades used in the sport of fencing, laid on the floor and stepped around

explanation.surface: Precautions to avoid walking into bits of a garden fence.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Highland dance the dancer steps nimbly between crossed blades laid on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish Highland dance is performed over two crossed blades without touching them.

clue.text: As judge. I am put centrally in place

indicators.note: the short piece is set in the middle of the other word, so put centrally in signals a container

parts.note: an estate is a place, a landed property
I am contracts to I'M

explanation.surface: A judge is being told where to sit: in the middle of the place.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity is to gauge or assess it roughly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Peter workin' in office that is guarded when closed

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
office work is typing, and the dropped G of workin' tells us to drop it here too

explanation.surface: Peter, working in an office that keeps a guard on it after hours.
explanation.walkthrough: A safe-cracker was a peterman in British underworld slang. The apostrophe in workin' signals that typing loses its final G.
explanation.definitionFit: This fastener has a cover over its point, so the sharp end is shielded once it is fastened.

clue.text: As the fourth, he took a name that was terrible

definitions.text: As the fourth, he took a name that was terrible

parts.note: the Roman numeral for four is IV

explanation.surface: A fourth-numbered ruler took a dreadful nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the Russian tsar Ivan IV, known as the Terrible, while IV taking A N builds his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixteenth-century tsar of Russia, fourth of his name, is known to history as the Terrible.

clue.text: Odd name put on individual pasque-flower

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
the word's letters are made strange, put out of order, so odd signals an anagram

parts.note: one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A peculiar name is given to a single pasque-flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges NAME to ANEM.
explanation.definitionFit: The pasque-flower is a spring plant of the buttercup family, a species of windflower.

clue.text: Sign on for some garden-rolling?

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run found inside it

explanation.surface: Joining up for a spot of rolling the garden lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To register or join a course or club is to sign up for it.

clue.text: Daisy's corolla

definitions.meaning: Daisy ... is the girl in the old music-hall song about a bicycle built for two
a corolla is the ring of petals of a flower, which may be shaped like a cup

explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy Bell (A Bicycle Built for Two)' is an 1892 British popular song; the possessive means the surname belonging to Daisy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup-shaped flower or petal ring takes its name from the ringing instrument, and Daisy's surname is the same.

clue.text: Heron is flying near the beach

indicators.note: the letters of the two words take off and land in a new order, so flying is the anagram signal

explanation.surface: A heron is seen flying low by the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Close to the coast, on the landward or sea side, is what this adverb describes.

clue.text: Soames Forsyte's daughter embraces an idler

indicators.note: the daughter's name holds the other piece within it, so embraces signals a container

parts.note: in Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga, Soames Forsyte's daughter is Fleur
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Forsyte Saga daughter puts her arms round a lazy loafer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forsyte Saga is John Galsworthy's novel sequence about a wealthy English family.
explanation.definitionFit: A flâneur is a stroller or loafer who wanders the streets with no purpose, an idle man.

clue.text: Material of a Norfolk jacket?

parts.note: a Norfolk jacket is a belted tweed coat, but read the county as the Norfolk Broads, so a jacket from there would be cut from cloth of the Broads

explanation.surface: Asking what fabric a Norfolk jacket is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in eastern England; the pun turns a fine dense woollen fabric into 'cloth of the Broads'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dense, smooth woollen or cotton fabric, a real textile used for suits and shirts.

clue.text: See the gathering?

definitions.meaning: run the two words together and they make seethe, to bubble furiously
a gathering is also a swelling of pus, an abscess or inflamed lump on the skin

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition only works if 'See the' is read as one word, seethe; the question mark warns of the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that seethes is bubbling hot, and a pus-filled skin swelling, or gathering, is the other sense.

clue.text: Sort of bed from which Hecuba rose dishevelled

indicators.note: something dishevelled is messed up, so the letters of the queen's name and the verb are untidied into a new order

explanation.surface: Hecuba, queen of Troy, got up from her bed looking a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the verb of the queen getting up but is fodder too; Hecuba was queen of Troy in Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A border of non-woody flowering plants is a common type of garden bed.

clue.text: Champion philanthropist helped to create records

definitions.note: the definition is plural while the answer is singular: discs cut in this material were themselves called by its name

parts.note: an ace is a champion, the best at something
Henry Tate, the sugar merchant, was the philanthropist behind the Tate Gallery

explanation.surface: A champion benefactor funded the making of gramophone records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helped to create' is link material saying the pieces build the definition. Henry Tate founded London's Tate Gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellulose acetate was the plastic of lacquer discs, and a one-off recording disc is still called by that name.

clue.text: Keep in mind what Archie Rice tried to do

definitions.meaning: to keep an idea in mind is to harbour or consider it

definitions.text: what Archie Rice tried to do
definitions.meaning: Archie Rice is the failing music-hall comic in John Osborne's play The Entertainer

explanation.walkthrough: Osborne's 1957 play, filmed with Laurence Olivier, follows a seedy British music-hall performer trying to amuse dwindling audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Harbouring a thought and amusing an audience are the two senses of this verb.

clue.text: What arresting strippers they were!

parts.note: strippers are people who peel off clothes or paint; arresting means making arrests, so think of the nickname for early London police officers, after Sir Robert Peel

explanation.surface: An exclamation about some unforgettable striptease performers.
explanation.walkthrough: Early nineteenth-century British police were nicknamed after Sir Robert Peel, who founded the Metropolitan Police; 'arresting' means striking in the surface and making arrests in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Old police slang named officers after Robert Peel, and anything that strips off skins also fits the name.

clue.text: Cautious about match in woody area?

indicators.note: the timid word goes round the match, so about signals a container

parts.note: shy means cautious or wary
a rubber is a match, a series of games in bridge or cricket

explanation.surface: Someone is wary of a game being played in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: A rubber is a set of games, especially in bridge or a Test series.
explanation.definitionFit: A planted area of bushes is literally a woody patch of garden.

clue.text: Tobacco tars condensed?

parts.note: tars are sailors, collectively the navy
something condensed has been cut down

explanation.surface: A question whether tobacco tar has been concentrated.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy cut is a kind of pipe tobacco pressed into cakes and sliced, sold under that sailors' name.

clue.text: Long live fresh air in places for raising animals!

parts.note: viva is the Italian cheer meaning long live

indicators.note: the letters are freshly arranged, so fresh signals an anagram

explanation.surface: A toast to fresh air on farms where animals are reared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges AIR to RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclosures where creatures are kept in near-natural conditions for study are the plural of vivarium.

clue.text: Brunel originally accepted a hypothesis of this sort

indicators.note: the jumbled name takes in the extra letter, so accepted signals a container
handled in an original, inventive way, the engineer's name has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel was the first to embrace some theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' rearranges BRUNEL to NEBULR, and 'accepted' then puts A inside it before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Laplace's theory that the solar system formed from a spinning cloud of gas is called the nebular hypothesis.

clue.text: Transfer funds illegally from Arundel

indicators.note: the answer is made from the place name's letters, so from signals an anagram

explanation.surface: Money is being moved illicitly out of Arundel.
explanation.walkthrough: Arundel is a town in West Sussex with a famous castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing dirty money through legitimate accounts to hide where it came from is the crime meant.

clue.text: Spare husband?

definitions.meaning: to spare is to keep back, not use up
as a verb, to husband resources is to use them thriftily

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean keeping something in reserve: sparing it, or managing it economically.

clue.text: Being agreeable, I would follow Simple Simon

indicators.note: the piece for I would comes after the fool in the answer

parts.note: a Simple Simon is a fool, a sap
I would contracts to I'D

explanation.surface: Someone agreeable happily trails after Simple Simon of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid means having a pleasant flavour, so tasty and agreeable to the palate.

clue.text: Not much of a round!

parts.note: a round here is a slice of bread or a sandwich, and the tiny crumb of one is very little of it, though round suggests a drinks round or a boxing round

explanation.surface: Grumbling that a round of drinks or a boxing bout was feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: A round is a slice of a loaf, and a tiny fragment of one is very little of that slice.

clue.text: A capital orchestra into the bargain

parts.note: the London Symphony Orchestra, based in the capital, is the LSO

explanation.surface: A city orchestra is thrown in as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: In addition, besides, as well: the phrase and the adverb are synonyms.

clue.text: Combed wool of animal upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned upside down means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lion is an animal

explanation.surface: Wool from an animal that has been combed and is hanging upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: The short fibres combed out of wool before spinning carry this trade name.

clue.text: A record salesman (retired) takes a walk in the garden

indicators.note: something retired has drawn back, so all three pieces are read backwards as one run

parts.note: a log is a record, as in a ship's log
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A recording salesman, now retired, strolls in his garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns ALOGREP right round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pergola is a framework of posts over a garden path covered with climbing plants, forming a shaded walkway.

clue.text: Put one foot in the water in Ely, for example?

indicators.note: the body of water is put within the bishop's seat, so in signals a container

parts.note: Ely in Cambridgeshire is a cathedral city and bishop's see
a pond is a body of water

explanation.surface: Someone dips a toe in the water at Ely.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is the area a bishop governs; Ely is an English cathedral city. 'Put' is a link word, and 'foot' is the poetic sense, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse metre, a foot of two stressed syllables has this name, so it is one particular metrical unit.

clue.text: Indifferent approach leads to date to meet

parts.note: dead, as in dead to the world, means indifferent or unresponsive
a line is an approach, as in a line of attack or argument

explanation.surface: A half-hearted approach still ends in a romantic date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' is the link saying the pieces lead to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A time limit by which work must be finished is a target date someone has to meet.

clue.text: Bird so excited by quarry?

indicators.note: the two letters are stirred into a new order, so excited is the anagram signal

parts.note: quarry is hunted prey

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bird is excited by what it hunts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' turns SO into OS; 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This fish-eating hawk is a large bird of prey found near water.
